key_insight: Small language models can be efficiently fine-tuned to produce high-quality, domain-specific relevance labels for enterprise search at high throughput, matching or exceeding the labeling quality of much larger LLMs while being far more resource-efficient.
problem_solved: Enterprise search systems struggle to get large amounts of high-quality, domain-specific relevance labels because manual annotation is expensive and existing LLM-based labeling can be costly and slow to scale.
method: Fine-tune small language models on domain-specific relevance examples to align them with enterprise relevance criteria.
Build an efficient high-throughput labeling pipeline (data ingestion, batching, and model inference) to scale labeling across corpora.
Validate SLM labels against state-of-the-art LLM outputs and/or human judgments to ensure comparable or superior quality while keeping costs and latency low.
impact: This enables organizations to generate large, high-quality relevance datasets affordably and quickly, improving search relevance tuning and downstream retrieval/ ranking without the compute and cost overhead of large LLMs.

paper_title: Fine-tuning Small Language Models as Efficient Enterprise Search Relevance Labelers
paper_authors: Yue Kang, Zhuoyi Huang, Benji Schussheim, Diana Licon, Dina Atia
